ĭn-expertus , a, um, adj.,
I.untried (not in Cic. or Cæs.).
I. Act., that has not made
trial of, unacquainted with, inexperienced in, unaccustomed to a thing: “qui lascivia inexperti advenerant,” Tac. A. 16, 5 : “exercitus bonis inexpertus atque insuetus,” Liv. 23, 18, 10 : “animus ad contumeliam inexpertus,” id. 6, 18, 4 : “dulcis inexpertis cultura potentis amici: expertus metuit,” Hor. Ep. 1, 18, 86 .—
II. Pass., that has not been tried, untried, unproved: “legiones civili bello inexpertae,” Tac. H. 2, 75 ; 1, 8: “fides,” Liv. 28, 18, 10 : “potestas,” id. 3, 52, 9 : “carmen,” new, Stat. S. 4, 5, 11 : “ne quid inexpertum relinquat,” Verg. A. 4, 415 ; Curt. 3, 6, 5; 4, 4, 2: “haud tibi inexpertum curvos deprendere mores,” Pers. 3, 52 al.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
